[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This batch covers 55 remaining US facility records for which this registry has no website on file, no dedicated operator-level research from any prior phase of this project, and no distinguishing lead beyond a short, generic, or highly ambiguous business or place name. Facility names in this batch include (by way of illustration, not exhaustive repetition of every field): 1GServers, 505 Marquette, Accelera Data Systems, Alembic Computer Services Inc, All About Serving Process Server, Allentown-TekPark, Alliance Technology, Arcola Tech Park, Argo Data Center, AZ Labs, Baltimore Technology Park, Cable & Wireless Cable Landing Station, Carrier Services Group, Datacenter, Data Center Lenexa, DataPro USA Web Development, Data Storage Centers, Digital West Data Center, Dynamics Mining, E-Foam, Emailage, ForceAmp.com, Geneseo Communications Inc, Insurance Exchange Building, Iron City No. 1 Power Generator and Compute Center, IT, J-Curve Technologies, K-Motion Interactive, Landmax Data Systems Inc, Live Oak Data Center, Marquette-Adams Telephone Coop, MDC, Menlo Digital MD-DC1, Minnesota Gateway Data Center, Newrays Two LLC Mining, OCOSA, Omnis Network, Open Data Centers Piscataway, OptimumHQ, Parsec Data Management, Pearl Plaza Office Building, Petadata, Precision Prints Lufkin Datacenter, Profit Finder Pro Software, QES Computers, Rack59 Data Center, Rad Web Hosting, Secure Data Center, Strategic Datasphere, Tennessee Processing Center LLC, The Chatfield Group, Thin-nology, VentureData, Vital Records, and Windbreak Cable.

Without a website, a distinguishing address, or any other lead in the source data, and with this registrys WebSearch tool exhausted for the duration of this project, attempting to attribute an operator to any of these names individually would require guessing at a real-world entity from a bare, often generic name (several, such as MDC, IT, and Datacenter, are single words or acronyms with no unique identifying value at all), which this registrys policy against matching entities on name alone and against fabricating unverified facts both prohibit. No operator attribution is made for any of these 55 facilities and none is fabricated; each remains an open research item that a future session with a working search tool, or manual human lookup, may be able to resolve.

reading.body:
The operator of this Phoenix facility is not published. The site is confirmed by OpenStreetMap mapping at a street address in Phoenix but carries no IT specifications, power capacity, or other technical data in the public record. Without published megawatt figures or rack counts, the campus cannot be evaluated on compute density or scaling potential.

Arizona has four facilities with published power specifications, totaling 512 megawatts. This facility ranks fifth by published capacity in the state, meaning it publishes no capacity figure while four other sites do. The state has 56 mapped facilities overall, indicating substantial real estate in use but little transparency on where power and compute are concentrated.

The absence of published specifications leaves this address as a mapped location without a measurable role in the current AI infrastructure picture. Until operator identity and technical capacity are published, the site cannot be assessed against the grid constraints that bind AI scaling in the region.
